title: argparse.ArgumentParser
summary: Build a command-line interface that parses, validates, converts and documents itself.
description: The reason to use it over reading `sys.argv` is not parsing — it is the free `--help`, the type conversion, the required-argument errors and the correct exit codes. A CLI is a user interface, and this is the one your users expect.
returns: A parser; `parse_args()` returns a Namespace of the parsed values.

raises.when: Arguments are invalid or --help was requested. Exit code 2 for a usage error.

examples.title: A small CLI
examples.code:
import argparse
p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Summarise a log')
p.add_argument('path')
p.add_argument('--limit', type=int, default=10)
p.add_argument('--verbose', action='store_true')
args = p.parse_args(['app.log', '--limit', '5'])
print(args.path, args.limit, args.verbose)

examples.title: Constrained choices
examples.code:
import argparse
p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument('--level', choices=['debug', 'info'], default='info')
print(p.parse_args(['--level', 'debug']).level)

examples.title: Testable, because parse_args takes a list
examples.code:
import argparse
p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument('--n', type=int)
print(p.parse_args(['--n', '3']).n)

real_world_usage: Every internal tool and batch job. The `--dry-run` flag on a script that changes data is close to mandatory.

common_mistakes.fix: You will reimplement --help, type conversion and error messages, worse.

common_mistakes.mistake: Calling parse_args() with no argument in tests
common_mistakes.fix: It reads the test runner's argv. Pass an explicit list.

common_mistakes.mistake: Accepting a secret as a command-line flag
common_mistakes.fix: Arguments are visible in the process list. Read secrets from the environment or a file.

performance_notes: Startup cost is negligible next to anything the program then does.
security_notes: Command-line arguments are world-readable via the process table, so never pass passwords or tokens as flags. Validate paths from arguments before opening them — argparse checks types, not authorisation.
